caveats: County match implementation instrument remains unresolved.

conclusions: This is a confirmed WEF-to-local-government financing and governance structure, not merely a networking relationship.
Public sources establish the state grant, grantee, vote, local-government partnership and project objectives.
The public record reviewed does not establish that WEF controls county policy or that every anticipated deliverable was completed.
counterarguments: The centre may function primarily as an industry-convening nonprofit rather than a policymaking body.
The county match may have been implemented through an existing Automation Alley appropriation rather than a separately indexed resolution.
findings: MSF Resolution 2022-080 approved a $3 million three-year grant to Automation Alley by a 9–0 vote.
The grant resolution authorizes final negotiated terms and requires repayment provisions for breach or failure to meet measurable outcomes.

The official packet states objectives including policy engagement, Michigan pilots, international networking, a Davos attendance opportunity, WEF intelligence distribution, co-branded events and reports, and three WEF staff resources.
Oakland County officially participated as local-government partner and announced a planned $3 million match, but the exact county appropriation or executed agreement was not located.
Oakland County's $10 million Project DIAMOnD implementation program predates and is explicitly cited as the local model the centre would expand upon.
David Coulter, Quentin Messer, Cynthia Hutchison, Tom Kelly and Francisco Betti occupy the strongest executive nodes in the local-state-host-WEF chain.
data.framework: Transaction-first public finance and governance analysis with separation of approved obligations, planned commitments, implementation programs and ceremonial participation.
limitations: The executed grant agreement and county match instrument were not located.
Anticipated outcomes are contractual objectives, not verified completion evidence.
Some current role pages do not establish continuity for every 2022 official.
data.method: Review official MSF minutes and board packet, state and county releases, WEF and host-organization records, and current role pages.
data.question: Which named people and public transactions directly connect WEF to Oakland County and Michigan government?
recommendations: Obtain the executed MSF–Automation Alley grant agreement, payment schedule, performance reports and compliance reviews.
Locate Oakland County's resolution, appropriation, contract or memorandum implementing the announced match.
Enumerate centre-funded Michigan pilots and government-policy outputs.
Identify who used the Davos attendance opportunity and Global Advisory Board seat.
Trace federal grant applications, co-branded events, intelligence distribution and TopLink access.
data.scope: U.S. Center for Advanced Manufacturing in Troy, Michigan, plus Project DIAMOnD as an adjacent local implementation program.
unresolved: Executed grant terms and measurable outcomes.
Oakland County appropriation and payment records.
Actual centre pilot projects and recipients.
Davos attendee and Global Advisory Board representative.
Federal grant applications and policy outputs.

summary: Official records establish a state grant, county partnership, local implementation program and named executive chain.
